name: Doodhpak
subtitle: rice simmered down slowly in milk until thick, scented with saffron and cardamom

ingredients.note: full-fat only; skimmed milk will not thicken

ingredients.qty: a generous pinch, soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk

prepNotes: Soak the rice 30 minutes, then drain and crush it lightly between your palms so a few grains break. The broken starch is what thickens doodhpak.
Rub the base of the heavy pan with ghee before the milk goes in. It is the simplest insurance against catching.
Steep the saffron in warm milk for at least 10 minutes so it gives up its colour.

steps.text: Grease a heavy-bottomed pan with the ghee and bring the milk to a boil over medium heat, stirring so it does not catch.
Add the drained rice and lower the heat to a bare simmer.
Cook uncovered for 40-45 minutes, stirring every 4-5 minutes and scraping the base and sides each time.
steps.tip: Scrape the sides back in as the milk skins. Those scrapings are what give doodhpak its grainy richness.

steps.text: When the milk has reduced by about a third and coats the back of a spoon, the rice should be completely soft and starting to break.
Add the sugar and stir 5 minutes. The mixture will loosen noticeably before it thickens again.
steps.tip: Sugar always goes in after the rice is soft. Added early, the grains stay firm no matter how long you cook.

steps.text: Stir in the saffron milk and the ground cardamom and simmer 5 minutes more.
Add the slivered almonds and cook a final 3 minutes. It should be pourable but leave a clear trail behind the spoon.
steps.tip: Stop while it still looks slightly loose. Doodhpak thickens a great deal as it cools.

steps.text: Take off the heat, grate over a scraping of nutmeg and scatter the pistachios.
Cool to room temperature, then chill at least 3 hours. Serve cold with hot puri.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated in a covered container. It sets firm when cold; loosen with 2-3 tbsp of cold milk and stir well before serving rather than reheating.
